Issues.Title: Button PNG images are rendered incorrectly (magnified or missing) in .NET 11, worked in .NET 10
Issues.Body: Is this a bug, or is it intended behavior resulting from changes made to WinForms in .NET 11? To reproduce the issue, simply create a new WinForms project targeting .NET 10 and .NET 11, add a button, and assign a PNG image to it. - With `FlatStyle = System`, the image appears heavily magnified and only a fragment of it is visible inside the button. - With `FlatStyle = Standard`, the image is not displayed at all. The same code works correctly in .NET 10. **.NET 10 (correct):** **.NET 11 (wrong):** **Video:** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26deac79-329a-48be-ad52-f9bbe4af4bf2
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Button PNG images are rendered incorrectly (magnified or missing) in .NET 11, worked in .NET 10" (#15427)

Issues.Title: Buttons should not use accent color when moused over or clicked
Issues.Body: ### .NET version 11 ### Did it work in .NET Framework? Yes ### Did it work in any of the earlier releases of .NET Core or .NET 5+? Yes. Only occurs when SetDefaultVisualStylesMode is set to Latest or Net11. ### Issue description The modern buttons when the DefaultVisualStylesMode is set to Latest or Net11 should not use the system accent color when moused over or clicked, inline with behavior in other UI frameworks such as WPF and WinUI - it should just change to a different shade of grey. Similar to other frameworks, the button should only use the accent color when it is the default button, like in WinUI for example, and in this case, should use it permanently, not just when moused over or clicked. Inconsistent (current) behavior when moused over in dark mode for example: Old behavior (similar to other UI frameworks): ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a new Windows Forms project 2. Use SetDefaultVisualStylesMode to set the mode to Net11 or Latest 3. Create a form with buttons on it 4. Run the application 5. Set an accent color in Windows Personalization Settings 6. Observe that the buttons all use the system accent color when moused over or clicked, but that no other UI frameworks do this

Issues.Title: Add ComboBox item editing and DPI autocomplete handle creation tests
Issues.Body:
## Proposed changes

ComboBox had little coverage for editing items and text against the native list, and the existing DPI-driven handle creation test only covered one parent type, one autocomplete source and one scale direction.

- Items: add/insert/remove/clear, `Sorted`, items added before the handle, `AddRange` with a null element, `BeginUpdate`/`EndUpdate`, and clearing a `DataSource` are all checked against the native list (`CB_GETCOUNT`/`CB_GETLBTEXT`) for each `DropDownStyle`.
- Selection and text: selection after remove/clear, `Text` per `DropDownStyle` (with and without a handle, case differences, non-matching text), and a single `SelectedIndexChanged`/`TextChanged` when selecting an item.
- DPI handle creation: nested parent, scaling up and down, list-items and custom autocomplete sources, all autocomplete modes, a `FontChanged` handler that changes the font again, and a later handle recreate. Each checks that the handle is created once, never recursively, and autocomplete stays initialized.

No product-code changes. A real monitor DPI change can't be automated, so the DPI tests simulate a mismatch the same way the existing test does.

## Validation

- `.\build.cmd -verbosity minimal`: succeeded, 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `System.Windows.Forms.Tests.exe --filter-class System.Windows.Forms.Tests.ComboBoxTests`: 976 passed, 0 failed, run five times in a row, non-elevated.

Issues.Body: Fixes #15419 ## Root cause UpDownBase uses the Opaque control style, which suppresses normal background painting. In classic button-layout mode, non-empty Padding leaves areas around the child edit and button controls that may not be painted, causing them to display an incorrect or stale background. ## Proposed changes Paint the clipped client area with the appropriate background color in OnPaint when classic button layout is active and Padding is non-empty. For disabled controls without a custom background color, use SystemColors.Control. Add bitmap tests covering visual styles, border styles, enabled state, custom background colors, clipping, and the Paint event. ## Customer Impact Controls with non-empty Padding in classic button-layout mode will render their exposed padding areas with the expected background color, avoiding unpainted or stale-looking regions. Controls with zero padding or modern side-by-side buttons are unaffected. ## Regression? - No ## Risk - Mini ## Screenshots ### Before ### After https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6577d422-c21a-4885-99a6-ea482828a885 ## Test methodology - Manual - Automation test cases - ## Test environment(s) - 12.0.0-alpha.1.26555.106 ###### Microsoft Reviewers: [Open in CodeFlow](https://microsoft.github.io/open-pr/?codeflow=https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/15420)

In OwnerDrawText mode, TreeView always requested CDRF_NOTIFYPOSTPAINT, even when the native custom-draw notification contained an empty paint rectangle. With TVS_EX_DOUBLEBUFFER, this caused unnecessary post-paint drawing and visible flickering.

Issues.Title: [release/11.0] Add opt-in native clipboard text fallback for WPF
Issues.Body:
<!-- Please read CONTRIBUTING.md before submitting a pull request -->

Fixes dotnet/wpf#11968 in conjunction with the corresponding WPF changes in dotnet/wpf#12125.

## Proposed changes

- Add an internal, default-disabled policy allowing WPF to opt into native clipboard text fallback. WinForms explicitly remains opted out.
- Support the opt-in fallback in the .NET Framework shared-core target as well. 
- Combine the original managed source with a captured native OLE reader. Read from the managed source first, then use the native reader if needed for `Text`, `UnicodeText`, and `OEMText`. For sources that don't support typed reads, typed text reads go straight to the native reader.
- For composed clipboard wrappers, forward single-argument `GetData` and `GetDataPresent` calls to the overloads with `autoConvert: true`, matching .NET 9. This also applies to non-text formats, but native fallback is still limited to plain text.
- Preserve custom-payload identity, managed format enumeration, and writes. Add six regression cases covering WinForms clipboard behavior before and after flushing.

<!-- We are in TELL-MODE the following section must be completed -->

## Customer Impact

- Enables WPF to restore Windows text synthesis when managed clipboard sources disable automatic conversion, addressing missing text availability and retrieval reported in dotnet/wpf#11968.
- Preserves existing WinForms behavior: unflushed clipboard data retains managed conversion semantics, while flushed data exposes Windows-synthesized formats.

## Regression?

- Yes - supports fixing a .NET 10 WPF regression. No intentional WinForms behavior change.

## Risk

- Low for WinForms because the fallback policy remains disabled. Moderate for opted-in consumers because shared clipboard composition and retrieval paths change. Native fallback is limited to plain-text formats and keeps the captured proxy's owning adapters alive.

<!-- end TELL-MODE -->

## Test methodology <!-- How did you ensure quality? -->

- Automated test execution and CTI manual validation.

Issues.Title: Fix #15352: Show selectable ContainerControls and their properties in the runtime PropertyGrid
Issues.Body: Fixes #15352 ## Root cause At runtime, `ReferenceConverter` cannot resolve unsited controls through the designer reference service or component container. It therefore returns an empty display value and a dropdown containing only `(none)`. ## Proposed changes - Add a converter that resolves uniquely named container controls from the current control tree. - Allow selecting a control again after choosing `(none)` and expose its browsable properties. - Preserve existing designer reference resolution and add regression tests. ## Customer Impact - Developers can see and select available container controls in a runtime PropertyGrid. - Expanding the selected value shows its browsable properties and updates them when the selection changes. ## Regression? - No ## Risk - Minimal ### Before The current value could be blank, and the dropdown could contain only `(none)`. ### After The current control name and available controls are displayed, selecting a control updates its expandable properties. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f0585e5a-ec25-4c20-a983-a0c72d4a8645 ## Test methodology - Manual and unit test ## Test environment(s) - .net 12.0.0-beta.26560.109 ###### Microsoft Reviewers: [Open in CodeFlow](https://microsoft.github.io/open-pr/?codeflow=https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/15408)

Issues.Title: Fix MonthCalendar test failures across midnight
Issues.Body:
Fixes test failures in build: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1671901&view=ms.vss-test-web.build-test-results-tab

Prevents flaky date assertions by deriving test dates from each calendar’s initial selection. Adds coverage for selection behavior with and without a native handle.

**Root cause:** Theory data captured `DateTime.Now.Date` during discovery, but each calendar initialized its selection later. When the run crossed midnight, the dates differed, causing incorrect expectations and a different selection-range clamping path. 

**Fix:** Derive relative dates from each calendar’s initial  SelectionStart  inside the test. This covers min/max date and selection tests, with and without a native handle.
